issue.title: feat(id-web): kitty-disambiguate-v1 rich keyboard encoder — Slice C of #787
issue.body: Refs #787 — Slice C only. This PR does **not** close #787: Slices D/E/F remain, and acceptance criteria 1–3 of the issue stay open until they land. Queue task 13060 (repo-health-code-pilot, lane code-j). ## What Additive rich/kitty browser encoder in `pkgs/id/web/src/world-keyboard.ts`: - New exported `richTerminalBytesForKey`, **unused by the UI** in this slice (inert, per design §6 row C). The legacy `terminalBytesForKey` and its tests are unchanged and remain the default path. - Escape is always `CSI 27 u` (never a bare ESC byte, which the profile decoder treats as Unknown); modified Enter/Tab/Backspace use their CSI-u functional codes (13/9/127), distinguishing Tab from Ctrl+i and Enter from Ctrl+m; Shift+Tab uses the canonical `CSI 9 ; 2 u`. - Arrows/Home/End keep legacy CSI letter bytes unmodified, `CSI 1 ; ` modified; Delete/Insert/PageUp/PageDown and F1–F12 (new in the rich encoder) use CSI tilde forms. - Ctrl/Alt printable scalars are CSI-u with the **unshifted** codepoint and the full modifier parameter (Ctrl+Shift+A → `CSI 97 ; 6 u`, which Slice A's decoder normalizes to scalar `A` + Control); AltGr (Ctrl+Alt) printable input stays plain UTF-8 text, as in the legacy path. - Same exclusions as legacy: Meta/OS shortcuts, Dead/Process/Unidentified, multi-scalar committed text, and profile-Unknown keys (F13+, modifier-only keys) return null. ## Tests Expectations mirror `doc/kitty-disambiguate-v1-fixtures.json` (the Slice A Roc `Key.parse_events` corpus); parity is decoded-event equality per design §4.4, and Slice D's oracle will decode this encoder's output with the actual Roc decoder. - `bunx vitest run src/world-keyboard.test.ts` — 20/20 pass (10 legacy unchanged + 10 new rich) - Full web suite: `bunx vitest run` — 667 passed, 9 skipped (30 files) - `bunx tsc --noEmit` — clean --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? issue.body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#77 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #181

## Summary

Four protocol gaps left after #61, each named in `docs/protocol.md` §6 and none tracked
elsewhere. Re-verified at `05c78b2`: **all four are still true**, and §6 still lists them, which
is the right place for them to live — a gap written down in the document that describes the
surface is worth more than a gap in an issue. What this issue adds is the ordering and the one
real design decision among them.

## Original notes

Not from the user's notes. Filed from the protocol work in #61:

> Follow-ups from the protocol work (#61), each named in `docs/protocol.md` §6 but not tracked.
>
> - **Questions raised inside `mcpx_exec` cannot be answered inline.** Correlation identifies a *call*, and a script makes many upstream calls, so questions from a script go to the broker rather than back to the MCP client as `input_required`. A script-level correlation (the run id) would fix it.
> - **Inbound `notifications/cancelled` does not interrupt the upstream call.** A client cancelling a long `tools/call` stops waiting; the upstream server keeps working.
> - **`notifications/tasks/status` from upstream is dropped.** mcpx neither forwards nor records it.
> - **`pool.callTimeout` is not call-scoped.** The most obviously wanted per-call setting: `--pool-call-timeout` on one command should bound that command's call, but a daemon started with a different value ignores it. Needs threading through `internal/pool` (#56 left it, reasonably).

## Current state (at `05c78b2`)

`docs/protocol.md` §6 "What is still missing" (`:368-382`) lists all four, plus two the notes did
not mention: url-mode elicitation raised by mcpx itself, and OAuth for remote servers ("declared
and not performed"). The last one is a #177 instance — a declared capability that is not
delivered — and should be cross-linked there rather than quietly carried here.

| Gap | Verified at `05c78b2` |
| --- | --- |
| Inbound cancellation does not interrupt the upstream call | `notifications/cancelled` is *sent* by mcpx as a client (`internal/mcpclient/client.go:715`) and accepted by the test servers, but nothing routes an inbound one to an in-flight upstream call. `internal/mcpclient/http.go:112` documents the decision: protocol-level cancellation was removed because `pool.callTimeout` was the bound that mattered. §6 states what is needed: "the request id plumbed through the pool". |
| `notifications/tasks/status` is dropped | The string appears nowhere in `internal/`. §6: "mcpx polls instead." |
| A question from `mcpx_exec` cannot be answered inline | §3.4's correlation identifies a call; §6 restates the consequence. Unchanged. |
| `pool.callTimeout` is not call-scoped | `internal/settings/registry.go:57` (`Default: "120s"`), read at `internal/config/poolsettings.go:43-44` into the pool's configuration. There is no per-call override path. |

## Approaches

Three of the four have no real choice; one does.

**`pool.callTimeout` per call — no real choice, and it is the one to do first.** Thread an
optional per-call deadline from the request through `internal/pool` and let the pool's configured
value be the default. The *only* decision worth making is whether a caller may raise it or only
lower it, and that decision is **not this issue's**: it is #185 (`ClampedBy` — a daemon sets a
ceiling, a caller may lower but not raise). Take #185's answer. A daemon operator who sets 120s to
protect the machine should not be overridden by a script asking for an hour; a script that wants
30s should get 30s. Note the interaction the code already documents: `internal/mcpclient/http.go`
removed protocol-level cancellation *because* `pool.callTimeout` was the bound. Making the timeout
call-scoped therefore makes the cancellation gap below more visible, not less.

**`notifications/tasks/status` — no real choice.** Record it and expose it. mcpx already polls;
the notification is strictly better information arriving earlier. It lands in the event store
(#6), which is where anything with a `seq` belongs, and #6's gap semantics apply — a saturated
consumer must see a gap marker rather than silently miss a status change. Do it with or after #6.

**Inbound cancellation — no real choice about *whether*, a real one about *scope*.** A client that
cancels and an upstream server that keeps working is a resource leak with a user watching it. The
plumbing is what §6 says: carry the inbound request id into the pool so the in-flight call can be
found and cancelled. The decision is whether cancellation is best-effort (send
`notifications/cancelled` upstream, stop waiting, let the server finish in its own time — which is
all the MCP spec promises) or enforced (also tear down the pooled instance when the scope makes
that safe). Best-effort is correct by the spec and cheap; enforced is what a user means by
"cancel" when a runaway tool is eating the machine. Recommend best-effort by default with the
teardown available where the scope is caller-private — which is the same isolation question #190
and #191 are about.

**The exec correlation gap — the one genuine design decision.**

**A — least recommended: give a script's questions a synthetic call id and answer them as if they
were a call.** Cheapest, and it looks right in a demo. It breaks as soon as a script makes two
concurrent upstream calls that both ask: the client is answering a question it cannot attribute,
and a wrong answer to an elicitation is worse than no answer. It also silently changes what §3.4's
correlation means, which is a documented wire contract.

**B — keep questions from scripts on the broker, and make the broker reachable from the client.**
Status quo plus a way for an MCP client to poll and answer broker questions in-band. No contract
changes, works today via `/v1/elicit` and `mcpx_ask_*`. The cost is that a modern client which
implements `input_required` correctly still gets a worse experience from `mcpx_exec` than from
`mcpx_call`, for no reason the client can see.

**C — recommended: add a second correlation level — the run — and declare it in §3.4.** A script's
questions correlate to the *run id*, which the exec surface already has and already exposes
(`execsvc.Result.runId`). A question raised inside a run is answerable inline by whoever invoked
the run, because there is exactly one of those, and the run id disambiguates concurrent upstream
calls without pretending they are one call. This is what the original note proposes and it is
right. It costs a documented change to §3.4's correlation rules and a revision-gated behaviour
(only clients that understand the run-level correlation get inline answers; the rest fall back to
B's broker), which is the pattern `internal/mcpserver/revisions.go` already implements for
`FeatInputRequired`.

Recommended because it is the only option that makes `mcpx_exec` a first-class citizen of the
question protocol rather than a permanent exception, and because the fallback to B is free.

## Open questions

- Does the run-level correlation need to nest — a script that runs a recipe that runs a script?
  §3.4's rules should state the nesting or forbid it explicitly.
- Cancellation and tasks overlap: cancelling a call that was promoted to a task
  (`/v1/tasks/{id}/cancel`) already exists. Is inbound `notifications/cancelled` on a task-backed
  call the same path? If so, the plumbing is smaller than §6 suggests.
- `docs/protocol.md` §6 also lists **"OAuth for remote servers. Declared and not performed"**.
  That is a declared-but-undelivered capability and belongs in #177's inventory. It is out of
  scope here; it should not stay only in a §6 bullet.
- Is `pool.callTimeout`'s interaction with `mcpx exec`'s own timeout defined anywhere? Two
  timeouts with no stated precedence is how the next "flag accepted and ignored" (#74) happens.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M overall — S for `tasks/status`, M for the call-scoped timeout, M for cancellation
plumbing, M–L for the run-level correlation and its revision gate.
**Impact** med-high — the call-scoped timeout is the most obviously wanted per-call setting in the
product, and a cancel that does not cancel is the kind of thing a user tells other people about.

**Related:** #181 (parent), #185 (`ClampedBy` — decides whether a caller may raise the call
timeout), #6 (event store — where `tasks/status` records belong, and whose gap semantics apply),
#112 (exec lifecycle hooks — shares the exec `Frame` ordering contract; #111 owns the rule for
adding a frame kind, collision 7), #177 (OAuth "declared and not performed" belongs in its
inventory), #78 (daemon state and caches), #56 (the settings pass that deliberately left the
per-call path alone), #61 (closed — the work these follow).

**In flight:** the PROTOCOL architect is working on these as this is written
(`internal/mcpclient/**`, `internal/mcpserver/**`, `internal/pool/**`, `docs/protocol.md`).
Re-check state before starting; parts of this may already be merged.

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

## Goal

Complete the remaining F13.4 presentation work tracked by #786. The shared bounded detector/profile from merged PR #5023 is in place; this issue owns the unimplemented tier renderers and acceptance proof, not another detector rewrite.

## Source and design

- Parent: #786 — Phase 13 F13.4 presentation capability tiers
- Design: [F13.4 decision-ready design](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/doc/2026-11-01_design_id786.md), especially phased steps 3–5
- Detector baseline: merged PR #5023 (5ad9688450c5e5dca36aee36002b11f71c59a770)
- Prerequisites #561 and #562 are now closed/merged; verify their landed behavior against current main before integrating.

## Scope

1. Implement Tier 2 cell-grid rendering and Tier 3 line-mode rendering for both SSH and interactive iroh TTY paths, retaining non-TTY iroh JSON-lines behavior.
2. Implement Tier 1 graphics/synchronized-output rendering behind the existing positive feature evidence; do not activate Kitty keyboard parsing or add guest-authored image payloads.
3. Use shared batching across all tiers, cell diffs for screen tiers, and text deltas for line mode. Preserve full repaint on attach/resize/invalidation and restore terminal modes on every exit.
4. Prove equivalent behavior using the same transcript-driven harness over SSH and iroh, including the three requested tiers, no-reply/malformed/interleaved input, byte-for-byte input replay, and no probe replies entering world input or the journal.
5. Record frame/byte comparisons against a full-render control and the F11.9 baseline.

## Acceptance criteria

- One harness selects and renders all three tiers correctly over both SSH and iroh from equivalent terminal transcripts.
- Every tier consumes shared server-side batching; Tier 1/2 diff parity and Tier 3 text-delta parity are asserted against the full-render oracle.
- No-TTY, timeout, malformed/conflicting replies conservatively fall back; unmatched user input is replayed byte-for-byte and in order.
- Non-TTY iroh JSON-lines behavior and unrelated SSH input/command behavior remain unchanged.
- Rich terminal sequences are emitted only after positive feature-specific evidence, and modes are restored on success, error, and disconnect.
- Reported output preserves the shell/journal contract; no capability frame or guest image payload is added.

## Out of scope

- Reworking the detector already delivered by #5023 except for a demonstrated integration defect.
- Kitty keyboard protocol work owned by #787/F13.5.
- New guest content, asset protocol, or unrelated terminal UX.

## Parent tracking

Keep #786 open until these criteria are met; this issue is the scoped implementation follow-on for its remaining F13.4 acceptance.

issue.body:
## Work (Drew, 2026-10-27)

The fleet monitor tends issues and queue state; nobody tends the
planning layer. Build `program-tending` (daily, all four repos,
≤~12 actions/run, everything logged):

- **Epics:** open `epic` issues — child progress, last activity,
  body-vs-reality. Silent 7+ days → status comment (last movement,
  next step, blockers); all children closed → completion comment
  proposing closure.
- **Roadmaps:** ROADMAP.md + planning/roadmaps vs landed work.
  Drift is fixed by PR (forward-looking rows only — never Done
  rows); ambiguous drift gets `meta/roadmap-drift` + a comment
  instead of a guess.
- **Projects:** board items whose status contradicts issue/PR
  reality get corrected where possible; unreadable board state is
  reported, never fabricated.
- **Stalled PRs:** open PRs with no activity in 48h+ (and no
  held/do-not-merge) get one check-in comment naming what they're
  waiting on + the next step; fleet-owned PRs that merely need
  shepherding get a `pr_shepherd` queue packet instead of only a
  comment. Drew's own feature PRs: comment at 7 days, never a
  packet.
- **Loose ends:** parent/epic notification when children close,
  duplicate cross-links, and the aging `user/review` list surfaced
  daily (his queue — reported, not re-decided).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Job live; first run's log shows actions (or verified
      no-actions) in all five sections.
- [ ] First roadmap-drift PR or `meta/roadmap-drift` application
      lands within the first three runs, or the run reports the
      roadmaps verified-clean with the checks named.
- [ ] A stalled PR receives a check-in inside the first two runs,
      or the run verifies none met the 48h rule.

issue.body:
## Problem

Agents open PRs and leave them. On 2026-11-22 the repository has 20 ready (non-draft) PRs opened by fleet agents and not merged. 12 have no unresolved review finding; 8 have findings nobody answered. The oldest is from 2026-11-19.

The job that used to finish these is `stale-pr-warden` (`doc/fleet-schedule-registry.md`: daily at 10:12, goal `keep-the-four-repos-healthy`). It files a `pr_shepherd` task per merge-ready PR. The last `pr_shepherd` tasks in the queue store are 17533 to 17535 (2026-11-16) and 20702 (2026-11-17). None since, while the registry still lists the job as enabled.

A task that produces a PR completes when the PR exists. Nothing then owns the review findings or the merge, so the issue stays open, its waiters stay blocked, and the branch drifts until it conflicts.

| PR | Opened | Unanswered findings | Title |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #11979 | 11-19 | yes | docs: publish first C5 efficiency report |
| #12008 | 11-19 | no | fix(fleet): refresh lock for atlas blake3 dependency |
| #12160 | 11-21 | yes | docs(id): delegation, transfer, and cross-signed identity |
| #12198 | 11-21 | not reviewed | chore(mcpx): collected run seeds |
| #12206 | 11-21 | yes | id: implement note embed views and reply anchoring |
| #12210 | 11-21 | no | Bolt: cache notification timezone formatters |
| #12211 | 11-21 | no | Palette: tooltip for the inline add-tag "+" button |
| #12219 | 11-21 | yes | fix(pm-dispatch): clean up task worktrees after session |
| #12221 | 11-21 | no | pm-stack: use current measurements for latest Explorer |
| #12225 | 11-21 | no | opencode-claimant: page /api/session within the 200 cap |
| #12226 | 11-21 | yes | C3 health hooks: wire opencode-working into lane launchers |
| #12240 | 11-21 | no | ci: register uncovered id integration suites |
| #12241 | 11-21 | yes | feat(id): add versioned MessagePack screen codec |
| #12246 | 11-21 | yes | feat(id): negotiate binary screen patches |
| #12248 | 11-21 | no | Palette: Associate image alt text with its label |
| #12251 | 11-21 | no | Palette: Preserve focus when cycling cursor modes |
| #12253 | 11-21 | no | Bolt: Index replay nonce expirations |
| #12259 | 11-21 | no | docs(atlas+pm): specify metadata schema v1 |
| #12269 | 11-22 | yes | feat(github-backup): add verified local cold bundles |
| #12273 | 11-22 | no | docs(living): accept P7 compute design |

Three of them are the plan's Now tracks: #12240 is step F1's registry half (#12230), and #12241 and #12246 are F12.11 (#805), one of the four items between `id` and its first release.

## What to fix

1. **Find why `stale-pr-warden` stopped filing** and make it file again. Its prompt lives at `/home/hatch/workspace/goals/keep-the-four-repos-healthy/crons/daily/stale-pr-warden__daily@10:12:00_user_current.md`. Check its last run, what it returned, and whether its dedupe treats done tasks as live.
2. **Make the producing task own its PR.** A task whose output is a PR is done when the PR is merged or closed with a reason, not when it is opened: answer or fix each review finding, re-check mergeability, merge. The root `AGENTS.md` "Finishing work" section already says what happens after the merge; this is the step before it.
3. **Give the sweep a fallback that does not depend on one scheduled job**: the coverage reconciliation, which already imports issues, also files a `pr_shepherd` task for any ready PR older than 6 hours with no live task naming it.

## Done when

- A `pr_shepherd` task exists for each ready PR older than 6 hours, checked by a query of the queue store against `gh pr list`.
- Ready PRs older than 24 hours: 0, for three days running. Add the count to `scripts/fleet/flow-report`.

Found by the 2026-11-22 flow review ([plan](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/planning/plans/2026-11-21_results-first.md)). That session merged only its own PRs.

Remainders of #10626 (claim-path staleness check, landed in PR #11799 and verified on main 2026-11-23 by lane GG — see the verification record on #10626). Two items were deliberately not part of that landing:

## 1. Filing-time state re-check (proposal step 5 of #10626)

Packet generators stamp `payload.issue.state_checked_at` (pm-stack console/dispatch write it), but nothing reads the stamp: a packet whose `state_checked_at` is older than a small bound (proposal: 1h) is not re-verified at enqueue. The claim-path check is the safety net and catches the class at claim, so this is source-side hygiene, not a correctness hole: generators should re-verify issue state at enqueue or stamp the packet so the claim path checks it first.

## 2. Criterion-6 deployment measurement

#10626 acceptance criterion 6: within 7 days of deployment, the daily work-failures recompute shows pre_done completions for tasks created after the fix trending to ~0, replaced by `staleness_autocomplete` events that consumed no session. The 7-day window runs from the queue broker running the #11799 code (broker generation 4, deployed 2026-11-22, is the first confirmed build carrying it). When the window elapses, run the recompute, cite the pre_done trend + interception count on #10626, and close it.

## First-tranche results (2026-11-07 evening, read-only audit)

Evidence file: `~/workspace/scratch/closure-audit-2026-11-07.md` (fleet-local).

**Part 1 — closed issues.** Totals: code 2,612 closed issues / opencode 939 / openchamber 845 / darwin-nix 840 (5,236). Verified the 200 most-recently-closed per repo tranche (darwin 60, openchamber 60, opencode 40, code 40) at the 766's evidence standard:
- 183/200 (91.5%) LEGITIMATE-LINKED (merged PR or closing commit on the timeline).
- 10/200 NO-EVIDENCE by linkage — all 10 read individually: **10/10 legitimate-by-record** (the closure evidence lives in agent-note comments: done-notes citing merge commits, supersession records, decommission records). Confirmed wrongful closures in the tranche: **0**.
- 7/200 DISPOSITION (not_planned/duplicate — incl. 4 "Scheduled Bolt" bot issues).
- Merged-PR "Fixes #N" spot check: 12/12 claimed targets actually closed, no negation traps.
- Closed-unmerged PRs: 326 total (code 206, darwin 55, opencode 39, openchamber 26). Sample of 12 most-recent per repo set: **12/12 closed as superseded/duplicate with a salvage note naming the canonical merged PR.** Zero silently abandoned in sample.

Methodological finding: linkage-only verification UNDERCOUNTS legitimacy — fleet closures carry their evidence in comments, not GitHub linkage. Remainder verification must read the record, not just the timeline.

**Part 2 — unmerged branches.** Remote branches: code 1,702 / opencode 322 / openchamber 221 / darwin 46. From the laptop primaries post-fetch, remote-tracking branches not merged into main: **196, all of them `archive/janitor-2026-11-07/*`** (the disk janitor's by-design archives; 0 non-archive). Local unmerged branches: nix 31 non-archive (mostly `queue/*` task branches, Nov 2–4), opencode ≥48 non-archive, code primaries hit the 100-branch listing cap with archives — full local census remains. Local "unmerged" overstates stranding (squash/merge-commit landings leave local branches permanently unmerged by SHA); patch-equivalence review is the real test.

**Part 3 — worktrees.** Laptop: 67 clone/worktree dirs scanned at ~/git top level + primaries. Named substantive holds:

- `~/git/fleet` (fleet repo clone): **1,556 dirty files** on main, no origin/main tracking ref — biggest single uncommitted pile.
- Small not-in-main commit counts (1–2) on ~10 queue worktrees, incl. `wt-id806` (design/id-806, #806 design work, Nov 1) and `devtoday-openchamber` queue/8357-224 (stale since Oct 22).

issue.title: feat(id): kitty keyboard slices E+F — SSH negotiation/framing and browser opt-in (#787)
issue.body: Implements the two remaining slices of #787 per `doc/2026-11-01_design_id787.md` §6. Slices A–D were already on main (Roc decoder #4438, assembler, browser encoder #7734, parity oracle #12926), and the F13.4 startup probe already records `kitty_keyboard` support in the SSH adapter — this PR wires activation to that evidence. **This PR does not close #787**: the issue's final acceptance also wants one supported-terminal smoke session (and the unsupported fallback) recorded against a real terminal, which a remote test run cannot supply. ## Slice E — opt-in SSH lifecycle integration (`world_ssh`) - New `SshServeOptions { kitty_keyboard }` (default off); `serve()` delegates to `serve_with_options()`. The serve command maps env `ID_WORLD_SSH_KITTY_KEYBOARD=1` to it, following the existing `ID_WORLD_*` env pattern, with a status line when enabled. - On a raw session (never command/explorer/exec), after the F13.4 probe closes with uncontradicted kitty support, the session writes the profile push `CSI > 1 u` + flags query `CSI ? u` and **verifies before admitting any key**: tokens assembled during verification are held; a flags report carrying the disambiguation bit activates framing, one without it — or a 500 ms timeout — pops the owned push and falls back to legacy chunk input with held bytes untouched. One attempt per connection (no renegotiation loop). - While active, input runs through the Slice B assembler: one complete key token per durable `Input` event, exact bytes preserved, split/CSI/UTF-8 safe. Verification replies are consumed by an outstanding-query-only filter — never journaled. Framing errors, incomplete token at EOF/deadline, and input-queue loss past the activation baseline are fatal to the session (no unsafe resync). - Teardown pops exactly the owned push on every exit path (normal, refused, error, cancellation) before the alternate screen is left. Form answers route through the same engaged stream so the assembler cannot desync around them. - The assembler module moves from the `id` facade into `id-worlds` (the adapter's crate); the facade re-exports it, so `id::input_framing` is unchanged. ## Slice F — browser opt-in (`web`) - `world.ts` selects `richTerminalBytesForKey` per connection when the page is opened with `?keyboard=kitty`; legacy stays the default. Paste, the manual input form, and Meta/Dead/Process exclusions are unchanged in both modes. ## Tests - `world_ssh::kitty` unit tests: flags-report grammar, outstanding-only consumption, verify flip/refusal, coalesced key order, fallback byte fidelity, split tokens. - `world_ssh` integration tests (real russh client + world event subscription): negotiate → verify → split CSI-u framed as one event, Escape vs Alt+x as distinct events, no reply bytes journaled, exactly one pop at teardown; verification-refused fallback (held key delivered, legacy resumes, no second push); no negotiation without the opt-in; no push when the terminal reports no support. - Web: new `world-keyboard-optin.test.ts` — DOM → WebSocket in both modes (legacy bare Escape `1b` vs kitty `CSI 27 u`, Ctrl+i vs Tab, Alt+x), paste + shortcut exclusions under the opt-in. ## Verification state (read this before merging) Remote dispatches were queued while runner surfaces were exhausted; all three were still `queued` (no surface) when this PR was opened. Handles (branch head `00520a8a3`): - Rust tests (`cargo test -p id-worlds --features ssh world_ssh` + `input_framing`): `fp_250be4a8258466cd46be42840fee197b` - Web tests + typecheck: `fp_b7b9a7f0f820ca7eb716a93e47b95c1a` - Clippy (`id-worlds`, `id-cli`, `id`, all targets/features): `fp_ac36488f6ba6798b5a8af6a3cba2b93e` The jobs are recorded in the fleet queue and run when a surface frees; results land under `fleet queue session result `. issue.title: fleet queue: add a repair verb for quarantined/malformed task packets (in-place payload fix)
issue.body:
## Problem

Queue task 18533 (for #7709) was quarantined by the claim path: its `payload.dedupe` lacks `checked_at`/`basis` (validation #5444), so every claim re-quarantines it. `quarantine-recheck` diagnoses it (`still_quarantined`, with that `last_error`) but cannot fix it, and **no verb repairs a task payload in place**. The only disposition available was cancel-with-disposition (done 2026-11-23; full record on #13091). The blocked pool likely contains more rows in this class — rows that read as "blocked" but are actually quarantined malformed packets.

What exists today (verified against the b8bbcc0 binary's `fleet queue --help`): `unblock` (incl. `--drop-dep`), `quarantine-recheck` (diagnose only), `revive`, `cancel`, `verify-disposition`, `dep-recheck`. None of them mutates a payload to fix a validation defect.

## Ask: `fleet queue repair <task-id> [--dry-run]`

A broker-side verb, sibling to `unblock`:

- Loads the task by id in whatever non-terminal state it sits in (blocked/quarantined; cancelled stays `revive`'s job — repair composes with revive, it does not replace it).
- Runs the packet validators and lists every defect it finds.
- Applies deterministic, semantics-preserving repairs for known defect classes. First class, the #7709 shape: a dedupe payload missing `checked_at`/`basis` is repaired by **re-performing the dedupe check live** — verify no other live task carries the same (repo, issue, kind) work identity — and stamping `checked_at`/`basis` recording that the repair verb performed that check at that time. If a duplicate live task exists, stamping would be a false attestation: refuse and say so.
- Repairs never invent content: an unrepairable defect (a missing issue reference, a malformed prompt body, anything whose correct value cannot be re-derived by performing the check the field attests to) fails with a non-zero exit, lists the defects, and mutates nothing.
- `--dry-run` reports defects + planned repairs and writes nothing.
- On success: re-run validation; when clean, clear the quarantine and restore the task to claimable state — queued, or blocked with its recorded deps intact — and append a timeline entry naming the verb, the operator, the defects found, and the repairs applied.

## Also in scope

Audit `unblock` against a quarantined row: before repair it should refuse with a message naming the quarantine and pointing at `repair`, not silently no-op or misreport state. Fix in the same PR if it doesn't.

## Tests (fleet-queue crate, named oracles)

- The #7709 shape (dedupe payload missing `checked_at`/`basis`, no duplicate live task) repairs, re-validates clean, and becomes claimable.
- `--dry-run` on the same shape writes nothing (row byte-identical).
- A duplicate-identity dedupe defect is refused; the row is unchanged.
- An unrepairable defect fails non-zero; the row is unchanged.
- A repaired task's timeline carries the repair entry (verb, operator, defects, repairs).

## Acceptance

- The tests above green in CI on main.
- A live `repair --dry-run` against one currently-quarantined production row, reported on this issue (read-only — no production row is mutated by the acceptance check).
- Do not change task 18533's cancelled state; it stands as the worked example, revivable later by an operator decision.

# Queue reprioritization programme 2026-11-24: full census, reorder, unblock

Ordered by Drew, 2026-11-24 00:50 CST: "review all queue items and prioritize reorder all the items. do two passes first to see where they are and bulk set priority/check for blockers second ensures blocked items are queued behind their blockers and the most impactful issues that unlock the most more queue items get pushed up. besides those general rules focus on new features in id the new features on atlas and fleet and pm stack then new mcpx features. tweaks improvements to existing bugs should all only get increased priority if they are important or unblock or have other reason to increase. prioritize designs they create new issues and unlock real implementations etc. maybe then do a third pass checking each priority band is appropriate. after first round do everything you can to remove blocked or parked claims. answer questions that shouldn't be waiting for me, resolve questions that were answers or made redundant or obsolete, handle basic needs triage and fix errors. go one by one through all of them for each pass"

## Predecessors

- #8876 — the 2026-11-12 reprioritization programme record (closed). This programme is its successor, not a reopen: same proven semantics (queue row is source of truth, GitHub sync after, failures to the outbox).
- #14100 — the `fleet queue reprioritize` verb spec (build = task 21658, in progress). Until the verb lands and deploys, this programme uses the November programme's direct route; if the verb lands mid-programme, the switch is recorded here.

## Priority law

HIGHER number = LOWER priority. Named scale only: immediate 5 / now 10 / critical 20 / urgent 30 / very high 40 / high 50 / medium 60 / low 70 / very low 80 / minimal 90. Aliases resolve on input, never written back.

## Passes

1. **Census** — every queue, every item: state, priority, kind, issue, claim/lease, declared blockers. Counts by queue × state × band + the blocker graph. No changes.
2. **Reorder + unblock** — one by one: (a) an item sits BEHIND its blockers, never ahead; (b) items unlocking the most other items move UP. Focus order for feature work: **id** features → **atlas** → **fleet** → **pm stack** → **mcpx** features. **Designs are prioritized** (they create issues and unlock implementations). Tweaks/improvements/bugs rise ONLY when important, unblocking, or another recorded reason exists. Plus claim/question cleanup: release stale claims on blocked/parked items (live claims never touched), answer open questions from Drew's recorded decisions and standing statements, resolve answered/redundant/obsolete questions, basic needs triage, fix packet/queue/blocker-reference errors.
3. **Band audit** — re-read every band, fix outliers, record per-band before/after counts for the whole programme.

## Hard rails

- Task 18533's state is never changed.
- Recorded hard skips stay exactly where they are (#1658, #2490 remainder, #9608 remainders, #2140, #13126 remainders, #13115 ask 3, PRs #13234/#13237, trackers #13240/#13241/#13264/#13272, #13178, #8583 remainder, #10910, #13506/#13507) — as does anything carrying a `user/*` label. The title failure — Magic Nix Cache throttling (HTTP 418) in run 45247507279 — is **not** what failed that run: the cache self-disabled at 19:21:26Z, the #774 mitigation (`fallback = true`, MNC `continue-on-error`) worked as designed, and the job ran 3.5 more hours before failing at 22:53:31Z on real check results. The throttle recurs (run 45369993004 today) and the fallback carries the run every time; no cache change is needed. In the nightly's targeted mode on main (run 45369993004), `id-clippy-lint>` and `id-roc-test>` fail with exactly that error, seconds in. With the parse fixed, roc-test then hit the two #787 Slice D environment gates fixed by (2) and (3): `key-parity-test.sh` hard-fails without python3 on PATH, and then without its corpus — both now provided.
